fleetMemory.text: A correct gate can be made wrong by a change that never touches it. `tier !== 'paid'` was exactly right for the 30 days there was one paid tier, and became a revenue leak the day a Solo rung landed. When a tier, enum, or status gains a member, every consumer that branches on the OLD cardinality is now a defect and none of them will show up in the diff. Enumerate consumers when you widen a union; do not wait for a reader to notice.

Seven comments across two repos described a gate that did not exist, and not one of them was wrong about the code. They were all wrong about the PRODUCT. A comment written from intent and never re-read against a later pricing ruling is worse than no comment: it answers 'do we gate CAD' affirmatively to anyone auditing by reading. Rename the function too — `requirePaidSession` was the accurate name for the wrong rule.

A three-state grant (true / false / absent) buys honesty at the price of a deploy ORDER. Absent must refuse with a DIFFERENT reason than denied, because a paying Studio customer shown a paywall is being told something false about their account. The cost is that the server half must ship first; declare that as a blocking condition rather than fail-opening to avoid it.

A mutation harness must assert its own anchor count. The first P-104 run aborted with 'anchor count=0' because hauska-map has MIXED line endings under core.autocrlf=true (files written by the Edit tool come out CRLF, files written by a python script come out LF), so a \n-written anchor matched nothing. Without the count assertion the harness would have no-opped ten times and reported ten passes. The convenient result was the one to distrust.
